chapter: Fats Waller, Nat Cole and Les Hite
title: Practicing rudiments every morning with Cozy Cole
summary: He says he learned from every drummer, especially Cozy Cole, a rudimental practice enthusiast who drilled him from the book daily.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Were black patrons allowed to come to the Famous Door?

Now you see, that I don't really know, because I could, you know, being a musician, because I would go to work with Cozy Cole almost every night, and any drummer that could hold the stick I went to hear him play, you know, because I felt as though that I could learn as much from the bad drummers as I did from the good drummers. I learned things not to do, you know, not to become sloppy and not to get lazy and you know, have pride in your playing. But I learned so much from Cozy, because Cozy -- he was a practice freak. He lived at the Dunbar Hotel; I used to meet Cozy every morning at 11 o'clock with my practice pad and my drum guide, and we would go through -- we'd go through the book together.

See, Cozy was a rudimental drummer, you know, and so he was a stickler for rudiments. And I think that basically, he really did help me because I'm not sure if I would have been as good as reading if I had not spent hours and hours with Cozy, because that's all we would do - just stay in the book, stay in the book.
